answer: EdDSA batch verification checks many signatures together by combining their verification equations into one randomized linear combination, so a batch passes only when every signature in it is valid. Each signature still binds its own public key and message through the Edwards-curve equation, and a random scalar per signature stops a bad one hiding among good ones. A hollow claim cannot shelter inside a marble batch, because the forge of the combined equation fails if any single signature is forged. A farm gains no cover from volume: one invalid signature poisons the batch.
